title: What roofers do
d: Roofers install and repair the weatherproof skin of buildings: asphalt shingles, metal, tile, slate, and flat membranes. It is demanding work at height in all w
description: Roofers install and repair the weatherproof skin of buildings: asphalt shingles, metal, tile, slate, and flat membranes. It is demanding work at height in all weather — and one of the best-paid trades for those who master it.

title: Essential tools
d: Roofing nailer or hammer, utility knife with hook blades, chalk line, tape measure, pry bar, shingle remover, caulk gun, tin snips, and a magnetic sweeper for n
description: Roofing nailer or hammer, utility knife with hook blades, chalk line, tape measure, pry bar, shingle remover, caulk gun, tin snips, and a magnetic sweeper for nails. Safety: harness, rope, and roof anchor — non-negotiable.

title: Key skills
d: Reading the roof: valleys, hips, ridges, penetrations. Proper shingle coursing with correct exposure and nailing. Flashing work — where roofs actually leak. Tea
description: Reading the roof: valleys, hips, ridges, penetrations. Proper shingle coursing with correct exposure and nailing. Flashing work — where roofs actually leak. Tear-off speed and clean deck prep. Estimating squares accurately.

title: Safety essentials
d: Falls are the leading killer: harness and anchor on anything steep. Heat illness — hydrate and pace summer work. Tear-off debris: watch below. Power lines near
description: Falls are the leading killer: harness and anchor on anything steep. Heat illness — hydrate and pace summer work. Tear-off debris: watch below. Power lines near roofs: keep 10 feet. Never work wet or icy roofs.

title: Getting started
d: Start as a ground helper or tear-off laborer; learn by carrying and watching. Many roofers go independent quickly — low startup cost. Manufacturer certification
description: Start as a ground helper or tear-off laborer; learn by carrying and watching. Many roofers go independent quickly — low startup cost. Manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning) boost credibility and warranties.

title: Pro tips
d: Flashing details decide whether a roof leaks, not the shingles. Never reuse old flashing. Ice-and-water shield in valleys and eaves. Photograph problem areas fo
description: Flashing details decide whether a roof leaks, not the shingles. Never reuse old flashing. Ice-and-water shield in valleys and eaves. Photograph problem areas for the customer. Clean the yard like a surgeon — nails in tires kill referrals.
